tagline: Up the gentle side of the watermelon mountains.
intro: NM 536 leaves the Turquoise Trail at San Antonito and climbs the east side of the Sandias through the Cibola National Forest, past picnic grounds with shelters, to a dead end at Sandia Crest. The road mapped here is only the top five and a half miles, from about the ski area to the crest. The Forest Service finished a dirt road to the crest in 1927. It was paved in 1960, which turned several hours of potholes and mud into an easy 45-minute drive to the ski area.
Sandía is Spanish for watermelon. The likeliest reason, by one account, is that the Spaniards who came to Sandia Pueblo in 1540 took the squash growing there for watermelons.

moments.title: Sandia Peak Ski Area
moments.text: New Mexico's first ski area opened here in 1936 as La Madera, with a 1,500-foot rope tow and two rides for 50 cents.

moments.title: Kiwanis Cabin
moments.text: On the crest between the ski area and the end of the road, hikers make for the ruins of a pueblo-style stone cabin built by the Civilian Conservation Corps above the Rio Grande Valley.

moments.title: Sandia Crest
moments.text: The road ends at 10,679 feet on a ridge with no true summit, where the west side falls away more than 4,000 feet in two miles to Albuquerque.

practical: Parking at the developed picnic and recreation sites along NM 536 requires a daily amenity fee or a pass.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Sandia Ranger District
